correctness.rationale: Verified each quantifier and exact step directly from the six frozen Git blobs. Both unitary and antiunitary conjugations biject the positive trace-class cone to itself and preserve trace norm; translation by P cancels in differences. For any positive B let X=B−P and Q support the negative spectral part X_-; for any positive trace-class correction C, ||X−C||_1 >= |Tr Q(X−C)|=Tr X_-+Tr QC >= Tr X_-. Choosing C=X_+ reaches equality (X_+ is trace class), proving pointwise dist. The negative-part variational identity, or 0<=Q<=I with B>=0, gives Tr(B−P)_-<=Tr P, with B=0 equality. Thus δ=Tr P. For any Wigner conjugation W, evaluating its approximation error at A=0 gives ||P||_1=Tr P, and W=U attains this uniformly; hence D_W=Tr P. At P=0 both defects vanish; at P>0 non-surjective range and nonzero Wigner error are established. No dimensional compactness or finite experiment is used: finite trace class has a separable spectral support even for nonseparable H. This is a correctness PASS despite decisive prior mathematical coverage.

originality.rationale: The advertised pointwise identity is the familiar positive-approximant projection theorem, not an independent new quantum-cone result: Bouldin (1987), Theorem 3, gives (B−P)_+ as a trace-norm nearest positive operator to B−P (normal, indeed self-adjoint). Thus the exact minimum equals Tr(B−P)_−, including noncommuting positive B and P. Dax (2014), Theorem 14, independently states the same positive-part minimizer for every unitarily invariant matrix norm and calls it not new. Once that identity is substituted, the remaining two global equalities are elementary evaluations at the origin plus the choice W=U. The nonseparable-H case reduces to separable trace-class spectral support, and the entire construction specializes already to H=C as x↦x+p. Resultary returns only the submitted item itself as a close match, but absence of an identically titled database entry does not overcome exact prior mathematical implication. Failure is originality, not alleged copying or author misconduct.

value.rationale: The motivation—testing whether the origin-normalization hypothesis in the finite-almost-surjective trace-cone stability theorem can be dropped—is natural. But the example is simply a translated cone, and already on H=C it is the half-line isometry x↦x+p with covering radius and distance from the origin-preserving symmetry exactly p. On general H the sole seemingly nontrivial identity is an old positive-approximant formula (Bouldin 1987; Dax 2014). Both numerical defects then follow in two lines by evaluating at zero. The final package supplies no additional classification, structural lemma, new cutoff or independently unknown exact invariant beyond a direct reformulation of that known metric-projection rule. Its pedagogical illustration of why zero fixing matters does not meet the separate mathematical-value criterion for a new research finding.
